abstract: Traditional volumetric electron microscopy (VEM) workflows fragment stitching, alignment, registration, and reconstruction across separate tools, demanding heavy manual supervision and yielding low throughput and inconsistency. VEM data further suffer from non-linear deformation, section loss, corruption, and illumination drift, while registration is slow due to the large image size. To address these challenges, we introduce the End-to-End EM Analysis Agent, an LLM-driven framework that unifies all major VEM stages into a single automated pipeline. By combining hierarchical deformation correction with context-aware slice recovery, it produces structurally coherent, high-fidelity volumes. The framework is optimized for Huawei CPU/NPU platforms with parallel acceleration, achieving up to$10 \times$speedups over manual workflows.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: UIGM: Segmentation-Constrained Flow Matching Model for Ultrasound Data Augmentation.
abstract: The scarcity of annotated data is a critical bottleneck in applying deep learning to ultrasound (US) imaging, a problem exacerbated by the modality's dynamic, operator-dependent nature. While generative models offer a promising data augmentation solution, they often focus on perceptual fidelity, failing to guarantee the anatomical plausibility required for downstream tasks like segmentation. To bridge this gap, we introduce the Ultrasound Image Generative Model (UIGM), a novel framework that introduces the use of a segmentationconstrained flow-matching process, further optimized with a non-uniform timestep sampling strategy to boost training efficiency. UIGM not only synthesizes US images efficiently but also explicitly enforces anatomical consistency by integrating a segmentation loss into the generation process. Experiments on three distinct US datasets demonstrate that augmenting training data with our synthetic images significantly boosts the performance of downstream segmentation models, outperforming conventional methods. Our work underscores the importance of task-aware data augmentation, demonstrating that optimizing for both visual realism and semantic accuracy is key to unlocking the potential of generative models in medical imaging.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: MambaME: A Mamba-Based Framework for Efficient and Accurate Joint Microstructure Estimation from Diffusion MRI.
abstract: Brain microstructure estimation using diffusion MRI (dMRI) enables quantitative characterization of brain tissue organization. Traditional dMRI models typically estimate isolated parameters, leading to fragmented interpretations. Recent deep learning approaches have explored joint estimation across multiple diffusion models, but often suffer from limited computational efficiency and accuracy. In this study, we propose MambaME, a Mamba-based framework for efficient and accurate joint microstructural estimation across multiple diffusion models. By leveraging the Mamba architecture, MambaME captures long-range dependencies in high-dimensional dMRI signals, enabling effective multi-model estimation. A joint estimation loss is further introduced to improve optimization across diffusion models. Experiments on the Human Connectome Project (HCP) dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of MambaME for joint Diffusion Kurtosis Imaging (DKI) and Neurite Orientation Dispersion and Density Imaging (NODDI) estimation. Compared with five state-of-the-art methods, MambaME achieves superior accuracy while providing$3-10 \times$faster inference than existing deep learning-based microstructural estimation approaches such as q-DL, MESC-SD, and HGT. Overall, MambaME substantially improves computational efficiency while also enhancing estimation accuracy.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Reconstruction of Absorption Coefficients for Quantitative Photoacoustic Tomography with Unsupervised Neural Representation.
abstract: Quantitative photoacoustic tomography (qPAT) combines the benefits of optical and ultrasound imaging. It reconstructs the quantitative distribution of optical parameters in biological tissues by detecting ultrasound signals generated from light absorption. The absorption coefficient ($\mu_{a}$) is crucial as it is linked to physiological and pathological features. However, in qPAT imaging, due to wavelength-depend scattering and absorption, the photoacoustic image reflects the product of unknown light fluence (LF) and$\mu_{a}$, rather than$\mu_{a}$directly. Reconstructing$\mu_{a}$from the photoacoustic image without knowing LF in deep tissue is an ill-posed inverse problem. To address this challenge, we propose a neural representation-based method for$\mu_{a}$reconstruction. This method integrates a diffusion equation-based optical transport model, taking into account the optical processes in PAT imaging to enhance the accuracy and robustness of$\mu_{a}$estimation. Simulated photoacoustic digital brain and phantom data experiments demonstrate that our proposed method can accurately reconstruct the$\mu_{a}$distribution, thereby enhancing the quantitative imaging capabilities of qPAT.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Task-Aware Functional Hypergraph Learning for Brain State Classification via Information Bottleneck.
abstract: Functional connectivity networks (FCNs) are widely used in fMRI-based brain analysis. While most existing studies represent FCNs using graphs, traditional graph structures primarily focus on pairwise connections, overlooking higher-order relationships. Additionally, many methods construct graphs or hypergraphs independently of downstream tasks, which can result in suboptimal representations that fail to capture task-relevant structures. To address these limitations, we propose a novel approach that integrates task-specific information directly into the hypergraph construction process. Our method employs a learnable groupwise mask to construct a groupwise hypergraph structure across all subjects. To retain task-related brain regions and filter out irrelevant ones, we introduce an information bottleneck constraint to optimize our framework. Furthermore, to capture personalized information, we design a hypergraph multi-head attention mechanism that learns personalized hypergraph attention matrices. We apply our model to the ADNI-3 dataset and ABIDE dataset to classify brain states associated with Alzheimer's disease and autism. Our method outperforms competing approaches.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: MAE-SAM2: Mask Autoencoder-Enhanced SAM2 for Clinical Retinal Vascular Leakage Segmentation.
abstract: We propose MAE-SAM2, a novel foundation model based framework for retinal vascular leakage segmentation in fluorescein angiography images. Due to the small size and dense distribution of the leakage areas, along with the limited availability of labeled clinical data, this segmentation task is significant challenge. To address these challenges, we integrate a self-supervised pre-training strategy based on Masked Autoencoders (MAE) with the foundation model MedSAM2. We further investigate several loss functions and identify a task-specific combined loss that yields the best performance. Extensive experiments and ablation studies demonstrate that MAE-SAM2 consistently outperforms multiple state-of-the-art methods, achieving the highest Dice score and Intersection-over-Union (IoU). These results highlight the potential of combining self-supervised pre-training with foundation models for challenging clinical image segmentation tasks.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Tissue Aware Nuclei Detection and Classification Model for Histopathology Images.
abstract: Accurate nuclei detection and classification are fundamental to computational pathology, yet existing approaches are hindered by reliance on detailed expert annotations and insufficient use of tissue context. We present Tissue-Aware Nuclei Detection (TAND), a novel framework achieving joint nuclei detection and classification using point-level supervision enhanced by tissue mask conditioning. TAND couples a ConvNeXt-based encoder-decoder with a frozen Virchow-2 tissue segmentation branch, where semantic tissue probabilities selectively modulate the classification stream through a novel multi-scale Spatial Feature-wise Linear Modulation (Spatial-FiLM). On the PUMA benchmark, TAND achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing both tissue-agnostic baselines and mask-supervised methods. Notably, our approach demonstrates remarkable improvements in tissue-dependent cell types such as epithelium, endothelium, and stroma. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first method to condition per-cell classification on learned tissue masks, offering a practical pathway to reduce annotation burden.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: OpenEEG: Uncertainty-Aware Open Set Learning for EEG-Based Brain Disorders Diagnosis.
abstract: Deep learning models for EEG-based brain disorder diagnosis have shown promise, but their clinical utility is hampered by the restrictive closed-set assumption and an inability to quantify predictive uncertainty. This limitation leads to overconfident misclassifications of both unseen disorders and challenging known cases, posing significant safety risks. To address these issues, we propose OpenEEG, an uncertainty-aware open-set learning framework designed to simultaneously reject unknown disease categories and quantify the epistemic uncertainty of its predictions. OpenEEG integrates a Transformer backbone with a UA-Classifier based on evidential deep learning, which learns a Dirichlet distribution over class predictions to derive uncertainty scores. We validate our framework on multiple public EEG datasets under subjectindependent splits. The results demonstrate that OpenEEG substantially outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both closed-set classification and open-set detection. By enabling principled rejection of unknown and uncertain diagnoses, OpenEEG represents a critical step towards trustworthy and clinically deployable EEG-based diagnostic systems.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Super-Resolution MRI Using Latent Fusion and Flow Matching.
abstract: High-resolution 3D Magnetic Resonance Images are important for clinical and neuroscience applications, but are timeconsuming. 2D imaging protocols can provide motion-freeze images, but their low through-plane resolution inhibits 3D analysis. Therefore, reconstruction of isotropic 3D MRI from low-resolution scans is highly demanded. Although diffusion models and latent space have been used in super-resolution reconstruction, how to build an effective latent space is still unclear. In this work, a novel two-stage generative framework is proposed, in which a 3D Variational Autoencoder (VAE) is trained on high-resolution images to learn a latent space prior and then fine-tuned to learn low-resolution image features. A conditional flow matching model is trained to bridge the distribution divergence between the VAE latent space and the space representing 3D high-resolution MRIs. Additionally, a latent fusion strategy based on gate maps is proposed to effectively integrate information from the lowresolution MRIs. The proposed method demonstrates superior image quality compared with existing techniques in both quantitative metrics and visual fidelity. Code is available at: https://github.com/yunzxu/LFFM_MRI.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: A Novel Dual-Stream Framework for dMRI Tractography Streamline Classification with Joint dMRI and fMRI Data.
abstract: Streamline classification is essential to identify anatomically meaningful white matter tracts from diffusion MRI (dMRI) tractography. However, current streamline classification methods rely primarily on the geometric features of the streamline trajectory, failing to distinguish between functionally distinct fiber tracts with similar pathways. To address this, we introduce a novel dual-stream streamline classification framework that jointly analyzes dMRI and functional MRI (fMRI) data to enhance the functional coherence of tract parcellation. We design a novel network that performs streamline classification using a pretrained backbone model for full streamline trajectories, while augmenting with an auxiliary network that processes fMRI signals from fiber endpoint regions. We demonstrate our method by parcellating the corticospinal tract (CST) into its four somatotopic subdivisions. Experimental results from ablation studies and comparisons with state-of-the-art methods demonstrate our approach's superior performance. Code: https://github.com/Hotel-Y/DF-NET_ISBI.git
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: MRI-Based Multi-Scale Multi-Modal Neonatal Brain Age Estimation Framework with Weight-Aware Feature.
abstract: Accurate assessment of postmenstrual age (PMA) is critical for evaluating neonatal brain development and predicting neurodevelopmental outcomes. This paper presents a novel multi-scale multi-modal MRI framework for neonatal brain age estimation that integrates body weight as a core feature alongside imaging data. Our approach leverages T2-weighted structural MRI (T2w) and fractional anisotropy (FA) of diffusion MRI (dMRI) employing a three-branch network to extract multi-scale anatomical and microstructural features from both modalities. A transformer module then performs weight-aware feature fusion, effectively combining imaging characteristics with clinical weight information for precise PMA prediction. Evaluated on the dHCP neonatal cohort, our method achieves a mean absolute error of 0.48 weeks in term-born infants. Furthermore, our analysis reveals significant brain maturation delays in preterm neonates, the degree of which correlates strongly with both gestational age and body weight. These findings demonstrate the framework's potential as an effective tool for assessing early brain development and identifying deviations from typical maturation trajectories.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: PROZONESAM2: Prostate Zonal Segmentation Using Sam2 and Gland-To-Zones Consistency Constraints.
abstract: Accurate prostate zonal segmentation on MRI is crucial for prostate cancer (PCa) detection and treatment. Traditional CNN-based methods, though effective in single-center training, often lack global context awareness and generalize poorly to external datasets, especially in the peripheral zone (PZ) with fuzzy boundaries. Recently, foundation models like the Segment Anything Model (SAM) have shown strong segmentation ability, but domain gaps and limited medical annotations hinder their direct use in medical imaging. To address these challenges, we propose ProZoneSAM2, a region-constrained fine-tuning segmentation method built upon SAM2. ProZoneSAM2 fine-tunes only the memory encoder and mask decoder (5.58 M parameters) and introduces a Region-Constrained Loss Mechanism (RCLM) to enforce anatomical consistency among PZ and central gland (CG) by constraining their spatial complementarity within the whole gland (WG). ProZoneSAM2 achieves Dice scores of 94.46%, 92.74 %, and 80.07 % on the internal test (from Prostate158, PROSTATEx, and MSD) and$94.37 \%, 91.91 \%$, and 79.96 % on the external test (NCI-ISBI 2013) for WG, CG, and PZ, outperforming CNN-based and SAM-based methods.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Energyflow: A Physically Consistent Learning Framework for 3D Microscopy Deconvolution.
abstract: Three-dimensional fluorescence microscopy images often suffer from blur and noise induced by the point spread function (PSF), leading to loss of resolution and structural fidelity. We propose EnergyFlow, a method for 3D microscopy deconvolution based on energy-guided flow matching. The model learns a restoration flow field along the continuous physical trajectory of degradation, while an energy consistency constraint enforces physical interpretability throughout the degradation-recovery process. This formulation enables image reconstruction without explicit inversion and achieves superior performance over classical deconvolution and deep learning baselines on both synthetic and real fluorescence data. The results demonstrate that energy-guided flow matching provides a robust and physically consistent framework for 3D microscopy restoration.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Brain-CLIP: An Individual-Preserving Contrastive Framework for Bidirectional Cross-Modal Brain Connectome Translation.
abstract: Understanding the complex relationship between structural and functional brain networks is essential for uncovering the mechanisms that govern brain organization. However, most existing studies model this relationship in a unidirectional manner, either predicting functional connectivity (FC) from structural connectivity (SC) or vice versa, while very few approaches enable true bidirectional translation between the two modalities. To address this gap, we introduce Brain-CLIP, a novel framework inspired by the multimodal contrastive learning paradigm exemplified by CLIP, in which heterogeneous modalities are aligned in a shared latent space through semantic correspondence. Similarly, Brain-CLIP aligns SC and FC in a common embedding space to achieve bidirectional translation. Furthermore, we propose an Individual-Preserving CLIP Loss that maintains precise subject-level alignment between SC and FC representations, enabling the model to capture individual-specific connectomic patterns rather than merely population-level correspondences. Comprehensive evaluations on two large-scale datasets, HCP and ADNI, demonstrate that Brain-CLIP substantially outperforms existing methods. (Code is available here: https://github.com/BrainX-Lab/Brain-CLIP)
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Federated Few-Shot Segmentation for Rare Brain Tumours via Weighted Aggregation and Prototype-Guided Adaptation.
abstract: Brain tumour segmentation is a fundamental task for neurooncological diagnosis and treatment planning. However, the scarcity of annotated data for rarer tumour types such as metastases limits the applicability of deep learning models. Federated learning (FL) enables multi-institutional collaboration without sharing patient data, yet existing approaches struggle with data imbalance, domain heterogeneity, and fewshot generalisation to new centers. We propose a federated framework designed for rare brain tumour segmentation that introduces three key modules: (1) client-specific weighted aggregation to improve fairness and stability under heterogeneous data quality, (2) a cross-attention decoder interaction to enable positive knowledge transfer between tumour types, and (3) a prototype-based decoder initialisation (ProtoInit++) for efficient few-shot adaptation to new centers. Experiments on seven multi-center datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms FedAvg, FedPer, and FedRep, achieving higher Dice scores and lower Hausdorff distances. Leave-one-center-out evaluations further confirm superior generalisation performance to unseen hospitals.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Brain-MGF: Multimodal Graph Fusion Network for EEG-FMRI Brain Connectivity Analysis Under Psilocybin.
abstract: Psychedelics, such as psilocybin, reorganise large-scale brain connectivity, yet how these changes are reflected across electrophysiological (electroencephalogram, EEG) and haemodynamic (functional magnetic resonance imaging, fMRI) networks remains unclear. We present Brain-MGF, a multimodal graph fusion network for joint EEG-fMRI connectivity analysis. For each modality, we construct graphs with partial-correlation edges and Pearson-profile node features, and learn subject-level embeddings via graph convolution. An adaptive softmax gate then fuses modalities with samplespecific weights to capture context-dependent contributions. Using the world's largest single-site psilocybin dataset, PsiConnect, BrainMGF distinguishes psilocybin condition from no-psilocybin condition in meditation and rest. Fusion improves over unimodal and nonadaptive variants, achieving 74.0% accuracy and 76.5% F1 score on meditation, and 76.0% accuracy with 85.8% ROC-AUC on rest. UMAP visualisations reveal clearer class separation for fused embeddings. These results indicate that adaptive graph fusion effectively integrates complementary EEG-fMRI information, providing an interpretable framework for characterising psilocybin-induced alterations in large-scale neural organisation.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: LIDSS: A Latent Information-Driven Dynamic Framework for Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation.
abstract: Semi-supervised learning has emerged as a promising approach to address the challenge of scarce high-quality annotations in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) segmentation. However, existing methods often suffer from limited segmentation accuracy due to difficulties in effectively leveraging labeled data, which stems from low tissue contrast, ambiguous anatomical boundaries, and a lack of reliable supervision in unlabeled regions. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel latent information-driven dynamic semi-supervised segmentation (LIDSS) framework. LIDSS incorporates three key components: an enhanced boundary refinement module (EBRM) to improve discriminative feature extraction along tissue borders, a confidence-guided adaptive replacement module (CGAR) that enhances feature learning robustness through an adaptive fusion mechanism, and a self-contrasting auxiliary training strategy to minimize discrepancies between dual decoders. Extensive experiments on the PROMISE12 and ACDC benchmark datasets demonstrate that LIDSS achieves superior segmentation accuracy and robustness compared to state-of-the-art semi-supervised segmentation methods.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: DBS-ElecNet: Automated Localization and Segmentation of DBS Electrodes in Clinical MRI.
abstract: This paper presents DBS-ElecNet, a deep learning framework for automated segmentation of electrodes and artifact regions in post-operative DBS MRI. To overcome reliance on manual annotations, we introduce a hybrid approach where a traditional image processing pipeline generates initial segmentations for the 3D U-Net model, which uses these as ground truth, and achieves robust segmentation performance. DBS-ElecNet performs inference in$\sim 3$seconds, a 60-100x speedup over manual segmentations. This efficient and accurate approach enables scalable analysis for surgical verification and paves the way for advanced clinical applications like artifact inpainting.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Strict Quadratically-Constrained Parallel Transmit Design with Unrolled Homeomorphic Projection.
abstract: Parallel transmission (pTx) has been widely adopted to mitigate transmit field ($\mathrm{B}_{1}^{+}$) inhomogeneities in ultrahigh field (UHF) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). pTx design optimizes subject-specific radiofrequency (RF) pulses under strict quadratic constraints for specific absorption rate (SAR) and power. Deep learning-based pTx design has received attention due to its ultrafast processing times compared to conventional optimization methods, but the incorporation of strict quadratic constratints has remained a challenge. In this work, we present an end-to-end deep learning framework for pTx design that explicitly enforces quadratic SAR constraints through an unrolled homeomorphic projection method. The proposed approach guarantees that neural network outputs strictly comply with RF safety limits, while achieving accurate and homogeneous flip angle maps without any postprocessing, substantially reducing computation time.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: MFD: Modality-Aware Fusion of FMRI and MEG for Noninvasive Speech Decoding.
abstract: Restoring speech from noninvasive brain signals is crucial for practical language brain-computer interfaces and understanding cortical language representation. However, noninvasive recordings still face a fundamental spatial-temporal trade-off: functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) provides fine spatial localization but slow hemodynamics, whereas magnetoencephalography (MEG) captures rapid neural dynamics with lower spatial resolution. To boost decoding accuracy, we exploit their complementarity and propose MFD, a modalityaware, two-stage fusion framework for continuous Mandarin speech decoding. MFD adaptively integrates fMRI and MEG representations, enabling cross-modal compensation between spatial and temporal features. Results on a public multimodal Mandarin dataset show that MFD consistently outperforms unimodal baselines in retrieval tasks, achieving 61.7 % top10 accuracy among 553 candidates. Further analysis indicates MEG representations better capture temporal-acoustic structure, while fMRI correlates more strongly with semantic content. These results highlight the complementary nature of fMRI and MEG and demonstrate the potential of multimodal fusion frameworks for neural speech decoding.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: A Multi-Modal Transformer for Ultrasound-Guided Diffuse Optical Tomography.
abstract: Diffuse Optical Tomography (DOT) is a non-invasive imaging modality that estimates tissue optical properties using near-infrared (NIR) light. Conventional DOT reconstruction methods suffer from poor spatial resolution and instability due to the ill-posed inverse problem. In this work, we propose MDOT-former, a multi-modal transformer that integrates B-mode ultrasound (US) imaging with DOT to enhance reconstruction accuracy. The proposed model employs a multimodal cross-attention transformer to extract morphological features from US images and improve the localization and quantification of optical properties. To facilitate model training, we introduce an in-silico simulation framework that synthesizes paired DOT and US data. We evaluate MDOT-former using both in-silico and ex-vivo experiments, demonstrating a significant improvement over state-of-the-art (SOTA) learning-based algorithms. MDOT-former achieves 95% lesion identification sensitivity and improves both structural and quantitative accuracy in lesion detection. The results highlight the potential of multi-modal deep learning in advancing DOT reconstruction for biomedical imaging applications.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Trialign: Pathology-Aware a $\beta$-Pet Synthesis From MRI via Disentangled Anatomical, Pathological, and Modality Alignment.
abstract: Detection of Amyloid-$\beta$($\mathrm{A} \beta$) deposition is critical for timely diagnosis and intervention in Alzheimer's Disease (AD). Although$\mathrm{A} \beta$-Positron Emission Tomography ($\mathrm{A} \beta$-PET) enables in vivo visualization of$\mathrm{A} \beta$pathology, its limited accessibility hinders routine clinical use. In contrast, T1-weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (T1w-MRI) is widely available but lacks pathological sensitivity. Recent MRI-to-PET synthesis methods intend to bridge this gap. Still, they often overemphasize anatomical differences and fail to capture pathology-specific signals due to incomplete disentanglement of anatomical, pathological, and modality alignments. To address this, we propose TriAlign, a two-stage$\mathrm{A} \beta$-PET synthesis framework that explicitly decouples these three alignments. In the first stage, a multimodal variational autoencoder enforces latent consistency between complete and PET-masked MRI-PET pairs, capturing anatomical and A$\beta$-related pathological features. Meanwhile, the decoder ensures modality alignment through$\mathrm{A} \beta$-PET reconstruction. In the second stage, a pathology-aware latent diffusion model refines pathology-specific residual between latent features of complete and masked MRI-PET pairs, guided by multi-scale anatomical cues and demographic prompts. Experiments demonstrate that TriAlign outperforms three widely used models in terms of image quality and$\mathrm{A} \beta$status classification.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Artifact Correction and Quality Assessment via Perceptual Contrastive Learning on Diffusion MRI.
abstract: Diffusion MRI is crucial for examining the microstructure of brain tissues, which are often affected by artifacts such as ghosting and motion distortions that hinder analysis. This work proposes a novel framework for joint artifact correction and quality assessment based on perceptual contrast. This framework integrates two stages of artifact correction and no-reference quality evaluation at the 3D layer level. In the first stage, we utilize an enhanced 3D U-Net architecture with Leaky ReLU activation and trilinear up-sampling. A hybrid perceptual loss function combining NMAE and HaarPSI is employed to effectively correct artifacts across 4D DWI data, yielding high-fidelity images. In the second stage, we construct a pseudo-reference by extracting low-level voxel-level similarity features and high-level perceptual features from the pre- and post-corrected data. Support Vector Machine techniques are applied to accurately classify images as artifact-laden or artifact-free, facilitating no-reference quality assessment. Our framework exhibits exceptional robustness across diverse acquisition protocols, outperforming existing methods and demonstrating superior artifact-correction capabilities. This research presents a reliable technical framework for automated quality control in dMRI, providing a strong foundation for subsequent clinical quantitative analyses. The code is available at https://github.com/yjh200319/React-QC_Artifact_Correction_Quality_Assessment_On_dMRI.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Comparative Evaluation of Five Hippocampal Segmentation Algorithms in Limbic Encephalitis: Addressing Inflammation and Atrophy Challenges.
abstract: Limbic encephalitis (LE) mainly affects the hippocampus, where inflammation and atrophy can complicate MRI volumetry methods. While manual segmentation is the gold standard, it is laborious and subjective, motivating automated alternatives. We evaluated five hippocampal segmentation methods-FreeSurfer, FastSurfer, SPM, JointLabelFusion, and nnU-Net-on 187 MRIs from 65 CASPR2LE patients and 191 MRIs from 64 matched controls. Expert manual segmentations served as reference, with performance assessed across accuracy and robustness metrics. FreeSurfer proved the most reliable, accurately capturing disease-related trajectories, whereas other tools were limited by crashes, training data, or anatomical variability.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: SFNet: Spatial-Frequency Collaborative Network for Fast System Matrix Calibration in Magnetic Particle Imaging.
abstract: Magnetic particle imaging (MPI) is a promising high-resolution molecular imaging technology that reconstructs images using system matrix (SM) describing the nonlinear response of magnetic nanoparticles excited along the field-free region (FFR) trajectory. Given SM is required whenever scan parameters or tracer changes, fast SM calibration is important in practical deployment. While sparse sampling enables fast reconstruction without a full-size SM, the predefined sampling grid often misaligns with FFR trajectory. This misalignment leads to incomplete and spatially inconsistent signal acquisition, resulting in SM distortion in both spatial-domain and frequency-domain and consequently introducing structural degradation and artifacts in reconstructed images. Here, we propose a spatial-frequency collaborative network (SFNet), which comprises a frequency-domain feature extraction module and a spatial-frequency feature interaction module. These modules are iteratively optimized to enhance cross-domain representation learning, thereby correcting SM distortion and improving reconstruction fidelity. Experimental results show that the outstanding performance of SFNet against state-of-the-art methods.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Hospital-Specific Bias in Patch-Based Pathology Models.
abstract: Pathology foundation models (PFMs) achieve strong performance on diverse histopathology tasks, but their sensitivity to hospital-specific domain shifts remains underexplored. We systematically evaluate state-of-the-art PFMs on TCGA patch-level datasets and introduce a lightweight adversarial adaptor to remove hospital-related domain information from latent representations. Experiments show that, while disease classification accuracy is largely maintained, the adaptor effectively reduces hospital-specific bias, as confirmed by t-SNE visualizations. Our study establishes a benchmark for assessing cross-hospital robustness in PFMs and provides a practical strategy for enhancing generalization under heterogeneous clinical settings. Our code is available at https://github.com/MengRes/pfm_domain_bias.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Cross-Attention Fusion of Structural and Deformation-Based Mri Features for Alzheimer's Disease Classification.
abstract: Accurate assessment of Alzheimer's disease (AD) using neuroimaging is important for understanding disease progression and supporting clinical research. Structural MRI (sMRI) is widely used for this purpose, but most deep learning approaches primarily rely on intensity-based features, which may not fully capture subtle morphological variations. Jacobian determinant maps (JSM) provide complementary information by describing localized brain deformations; however, conventional multimodal fusion strategies such as early or late fusion may not fully capture the interactions between these modalities. To address this, we explore a cross-attention fusion approach that explicitly models the relationship between sMRI intensity and JSM-derived deformation features for AD classification. Using data from the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), we compare cross-attention with pairwise self-attention and four baseline fusion methods. The proposed approach achieved mean ROC-AUC scores of 0.903 (0.033) for AD vs. cognitively normal (CN) and 0.692 (0.061) for mild cognitive impairment (MCI) vs. CN under five-fold cross-validation. The proposed approach achieved the best performance among fusion strategies and achieved higher or comparable performance with only 1.56 million parameters. These findings suggest that cross-attention fusion may serve as a potentially useful approach for integrating structural and deformation-based MRI features in AD classification tasks.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Cortical Surface-Constrained Temporally Continuous Atlas Learning for Fetal Brain MRI.
abstract: Constructing a temporally continuous fetal brain atlas with anatomically realistic cortical geometry remains challenging due to rapid cortical folding during gestation. Deep learning, especially Implicit Neural Representation (INR) based methods, improves continuity but often fails to ensure cortical alignment due to the absence of explicit geometric constraints. We propose a cortical surface-constrained joint learning framework that integrates a registration network with an INR for continuous atlas representation. The registration network learns accurate deformation fields, while surface constraints guide alignment to preserve cortical topology. Through joint optimization, our method constructs a temporally continuous fetal brain atlas that captures smooth developmental transitions and preserves anatomically faithful cortical folding. Experiments on the dHCP dataset demonstrate that our method produces anatomically consistent and temporally smooth 4D atlases, achieving superior label-propagation (atlas-based) segmentation accuracy and biologically plausible developmental trajectories.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: FMIR, A Foundation Model-Based Image Registration Framework for Robust Image Registration.
abstract: Deep learning has revolutionized medical image registration by achieving unprecedented speeds, yet its clinical application is hindered by a limited ability to generalize beyond the training domain, a critical weakness given the typically small scale of medical datasets. In this paper, we introduce FMIR, a foundation model-based registration framework that overcomes this limitation. Combining a foundation model-based feature encoder for extracting anatomical structures with a general registration head, and trained with a channel regularization strategy on just a single dataset, FMIR achieves state-of-the-art(SOTA) in-domain performance while maintaining robust registration on out-of-domain images. Our approach demonstrates a viable path toward building generalizable medical imaging foundation models with limited resources. The source code will be released upon acceptance.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Pretext Task Adversarial Learning for Unpaired Low-Field to Ultra High-Field MRI Synthesis.
abstract: Given the scarcity and high cost of high-field MRI, synthesizing high-field images from low-field MRI offers great potential for augmenting limited data in downstream tasks (e.g., segmentation). Low-field MRI typically suffers from low SNR and spatial resolution, making cross-domain synthesis challenging due to feature misalignment and anatomical distortion. To address this, we propose a Pretext Task Adversarial (PTA) framework for high-field MRI synthesis. It consists of: (1) a Slice-wise Gap Perception (SGP) network for aligning inter-slice inconsistencies via contrastive learning; (2) a Local Structure Correction (LSC) network for refining local details from rotated and masked inputs; and (3) a pretext-guided adversarial training that enhances realism through additional supervision and discrimination. Experiments on low-to-ultra-high-field MRI demonstrate state-of-the-art performance (FID =16.892, IS =1.933, MS-SSIM =0.324), generating anatomically consistent high-field-like data to improve downstream training. The code is available at: https://github.com/Zhenxuan-Zhang/PTA4Unpaired_HF_MRI_SYN.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Log Focal Frequency Loss for Bioimage Restoration.
abstract: Image restoration of biological structures in microscopy poses unique challenges for preserving fine textures and sharp edges. While recent GAN-based image restoration formulations have introduced frequency-domain losses for natural images, microscopy images pose distinct challenges with large dynamic ranges and sparse but critical structures with spatially-variable contrast. Inspired by the principle of logarithmic perception in human vision, we propose a log focal frequency loss (LFFL) tailored for microscopy restoration. This loss combines adaptive spectral weighting from log-space differences with log-dampened error measurement, ensuring balanced reconstruction across all frequency bands while preserving both structural coherence and fine details. We tested our GAN-based framework on two use-cases with real ground-truths: deblurring of fluorescence images of cell nuclei on microgroove substrates and denoising of zebrafish embryo images from the FMD dataset. Compared to training with only spatial-domain losses and with existing frequencydomain losses, our method achieves improvements across several quality metrics. Code is available at github.com/xjzhaang/log-focal-frequency-loss.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Integrating Population and Individual Brain Network with Mixture-of-Experts for Mild Cognitive Impairment Study.
abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) diagnosis from neuroimaging requires a comprehensive understanding of brain connectivity patterns. While multi-atlas approaches provide complementary perspectives on brain organization, existing methods rely predominantly on functional connectivity and employ static fusion strategies that introduce information redundancy. To address this, we propose a novel framework that integrates individualized three-hinge gyrus (3 HG) -based brain networks with population-level atlases based networks through a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture. Specifically, brain graph encoders extract structural and functional connectivity embeddings from each atlas, which are processed by atlas-shared and atlas-specific experts to learn atlas-shared and atlas-specific brain patterns, respectively. A gating mechanism dynamically weighs expert contributions, enabling adaptive cross-atlas fusion. Evaluations on the ADNI demonstrate that our method achieves superior performance while providing interpretable insights into atlas-specific diagnostic contributions. Code is available at: https://github.com/Nancy-Zhang-0/Multi-Atlas-MoE
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Sam-Peft: a Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Framework Fusing Multi-Modal Mri for Prompt-Free Glioma Segmentation.
abstract: Accurate glioma delineation on multi-modal MRI is pivotal for clinical planning, yet remains difficult in practice: cross-site fusion of T1, T1Gd, T2, and FLAIR is brittle, routine pipelines lack manual point/box prompts, and fully fine-tuning large backbones is compute-intensive. In this paper, we present SAM-PEFT, a promptfree, parameter-efficient adaptation of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for multi-modal MRI glioma segmentation. SAM-PEFT freezes the SAM backbone and adds: (i) a Multi-Modal Feature Adaptive Fusion (MFAM) for T1, T1Gd, T2, and FLAIR integration; (ii) a Lightweight Prompt Encoder (LPE) with efficient anatomical positional encoding to generate dense internal prompts; and (iii) TransMedAttention for fine-grained refinement. Training only$\sim 5.8 \%$of the model parameters, SAM-PEFT attains a mean Dice of 0.9151 on a held-out test split of the BraTS 2025 preoperative subset, matching or exceeding strong CNN/Transformer baselines and SAM variants. These results suggest a practical route to adapt foundation models to clinical MRI segmentation with modest compute.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Lost in Distortion: Uncovering the Domain Gap Between Computer Vision and Brain Imaging - a Study on Pretraining for Age Prediction.
abstract: Large-scale brain imaging datasets provide unprecedented opportunities for developing domain foundation models through pretraining. However, unlike natural image datasets in computer vision, these neuroimaging data often exhibit high heterogeneity in quality, ranging from well-structured scans to severely distorted or incomplete brain volumes. This raises a fundamental question: can noise or low-quality scans contribute meaningfully to pretraining, or do they instead hinder model learning? In this study, we systematically explore the role of data quality level in pretraining and its impact on downstream tasks. Specifically, we perform pretraining on datasets with different quality levels and perform fine-tuning for brain age prediction on external cohorts. Our results show significant performance differences across quality levels, revealing both opportunities and limitations. We further discuss the gap between computer vision practices and clinical neuroimaging standards, emphasizing the necessity of domain-aware curation to ensure trusted and generalizable domain-specific foundation models.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Two-Stage Physics-Guided Self-Supervised Quantitative MRI with Diffusion-Based Refinement for Synthetic DIR Imaging in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Quantitative mapping and double inversion recovery (DIR) imaging enhance lesion visibility in multiple sclerosis (MS) but are limited by long, non-routine acquisition times. We propose a physics-guided self-supervised framework to estimate T1, T2, and PD maps directly from standard clinical scans (T1w, T2w, and FLAIR). Stage 1 utilizes a conditional GAN to generate pseudo-quantitative maps constrained by Bloch-based forward modeling, enabling training without paired labels. Stage 2 leverages these pseudo-labels to learn a conditional diffusion prior, followed by physics-consistency posterior sampling to derive high-fidelity quantitative maps. Evaluation on 50 MS patients demonstrates that our twostage approach significantly outperforms GAN-only baselines, achieving up to +28 dB PSNR gain and near-perfect structural agreement (SSIM$\approx 0.999$). The refined maps enable high-quality DIR synthesis with superior cortical lesion visibility, offering a practical, acquisition-free strategy for quantitative MRI within routine clinical protocols.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Task-Oriented Uncertainty Collaborative Learning for Label-Efficient Brain Tumor Segmentation.
abstract: Multi-contrast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) enhances brain tumour segmentation by combining complementary tissue information from different contrasts. Yet, existing approaches struggle with multi-level specificity perception and data heterogeneity, particularly under limited annotations. We propose a Task-oriented Uncertainty Collaborative Learning (TUCL) framework that integrates a task-oriented prompt attention (TPA) module and a dual-path uncertainty refinement (DUR) strategy for robust multi-contrast segmentation. TPA employs intra- and cross-prompt attention to model inter-contrast dependencies, while DUR iteratively refines predictions through uncertainty feedback. Evaluated on limited-label MRI data, TUCL achieves a Dice score of 88.2 % and HD95 of 10.853 mm, demonstrating strong generalisation and reduced reliance on extensive annotations. Code: https://github.com/Zhenxuan-Zhang/TUCL_BrainSeg
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: AutoATQ: Automating Along-Tract Quantification Without Tractography.
abstract: Diffusion MRI (dMRI) is a unique noninvasive technique for characterizing brain white-matter microstructure, and tractometry is a key analytical method for identifying localized abnormalities. However, traditional tractometry relies on tractography, which has significant limitations, including indirect inference of anatomy, false-positive streamlines, and difficulties with crossing fibers. Additionally, it requires a lengthy acquisition of$q$-space data. To this end, we propose a novel deep learning framework for direct microstructural characterization using white matter bundle masks, thereby eliminating the need for tractography. Our approach uses the U-Mamba network to accurately segment 72 predefined white matter bundles from parameterized spherical mean images, thereby enhancing tissue specificity. We also introduce a dedicated point cloud network to estimate the centerline of each tract and aggregate voxel-wise microstructural features for detailed analysis. Experimental results show that our framework's profiles align closely with those from the established along-tract analytics. Ultimately, we offer a more robust and efficient tractometric solution that advances the clinical use of dMRI and facilitates large-scale neuroimaging studies. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/Zhang-Chengzhe/AutoATQ.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Disdiff: Self-Supervised Segmentation on Histopathology Images Using Diffusion Models and Distance Maps.
abstract: Histopathological image segmentation is crucial for clinical diagnosis, but obtaining high-quality annotations is timeconsuming and labor-intensive. To improve segmentation performance while reducing annotation dependence, this paper presents DisDiff, a novel two-stage self-supervised framework leveraging diffusion models for nuclei segmentation without pseudo-labels. In the first stage, a Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model (DDPM) with Perception Prioritized (P2) weighting learns robust features from unlabeled images. In the second stage, pretrained weights are transferred to a U-Net enhanced with Efficient Multi-scale Attention (EMA) and distance map post-processing for effective nuclei separation. Experiments on TCGA and TNBC datasets show that DisDiff achieves competitive performance with only 50 % labeled data and superior results with full annotations, demonstrating practical value for clinical applications.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Foundation Model-Guided Iteratively Prompting and Pseudo-Labeling for Partially Labeled Medical Image Segmentation.
abstract: Automated medical image segmentation has achieved remarkable progress with fully labeled data. However, sitespecific clinical priorities and the high cost of manual annotation often yield scans with only a subset of organs labeled, leading to the partially labeled problem that degrades performance. To address this issue, we propose IPnP, an Iteratively Prompting and Pseudo-labeling framework, for partially labeled medical image segmentation. IPnP iteratively generates and refines pseudo-labels for unlabeled organs through collaboration between a trainable segmentation network (specialist) and a frozen foundation model (generalist), progressively recovering full-organ supervision. On the public dataset AMOS with the simulated partial-label setting, IPnP consistently improves segmentation performance over prior methods and approaches the performance of the fully labeled reference. We further evaluate on a private, partially labeled dataset of 210 head-and-neck cancer patients and demonstrate our effectiveness in real-world clinical settings.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: A Pipeline for DTI Indices and Connectivity Analysis Applied to a Longitudinal Multiple Sclerosis Cohort.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) causes progressive white matter damage, which can be sensitively assessed using diffusion MRI. However, existing analyses often rely on manual delineation, limiting scalability. We present an automated diffusion-MRI pipeline that computes global lesion-averaged DTI indices, tract-specific measures within tract-lesion intersections, and whole-brain structural connectivity metrics without manual intervention. The framework integrates lesion segmentation and filling, DWI preprocessing and DTI index computation, tractography reconstruction, bundle extraction, brain network analysis, and statistical analysis. Applied to a longitudinal MS cohort, the pipeline produced diffusion and connectivity patterns consistent with previously reported trends, supporting its validity. These results demonstrate the feasibility and practical utility of the proposed framework for scalable, longitudinal MS analysis.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Fedharmo: Harmonizing Global Aggregation and Local Alignment in Cross-Domain Federated Medical Image Segmentation.
abstract: Federated learning has emerged as the mainstream technique for breaking data silos in the healthcare domain by enabling collaborative training of machine learning models among different clients while ensuring data privacy. However, due to the discrepancy in the data distribution of each client, the aggregated model may ultimately be shifted towards certain clients. Consequently, we propose FedHarmo, a federated learning segmentation framework that employs an adaptive aggregation weight updating strategy to prevent model aggregation shifted towards certain clients. Additionally, we utilize the distribution measurement metric to minimize the distance between the global model and local models. Comprehensive experiments on ten medical image datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method. Our code are available at https://github.com/GGbond-study/FedHarmo.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: DiSMemNet: Structure-Aware Distillation and Memory Network for Generalizable Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in EM Segmentation.
abstract: Deep learning has greatly advanced electron microscopy (EM) segmentation, yet supervised models remain limited by costly voxel annotations and poor generalization across datasets with large domain shifts in contrast, texture, and morphology. These discrepancies distort both appearance and organelle topology, making structure-preserving adaptation essential for reliable EM analysis. To address this challenge, we propose DiSMemNet, a unified framework for unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) that jointly enhances appearance-structure alignment and cross-domain generalization. The framework consists of two synergistic modules: a gated contrastive translation module that preserves morphological continuity during adversarial alignment, and a distillation-memory synergy module that stabilizes pseudo-label learning via multi-scale distillation and prototype-guided refinement. Through unified optimization of semantic, structural, and appearance consistency, DiSMemNet achieves topology-preserving adaptation and stable convergence across diverse EM domains. Extensive experiments on MitoADWT, SynADWT, and Lucchi datasets demonstrate that DiSMemNet achieves state-of-the-art performance, yielding sharper boundaries, continuous structures, and strong generalization without target annotations. The results highlight its potential as a structure-aware and domainrobust framework for large-scale EM segmentation. Our code is available at https://github.com/RNZhou0529/DiSMemNet.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Deep-Learning Cortical Registration Guided by Structural and Diffusion MRI and Connectivity.
abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate cortical surface registration is crucial for group-level neuroimaging analyses, yet geometry-based methods often yield suboptimal functional alignment across subjects due to substantial inter-individual variability. We present a novel deep-learning approach that incorporates white matter structural connectivity features from diffusion MRI (dMRI) tractography into the Joint Surface-based Registration and Atlas Construction (JOSA) framework. Our method generates vertex-wise connectivity maps by detecting streamline-surface intersections, followed by heat diffusion smoothing on the cortical manifold. We combine these connectivity features with scalar diffusion metrics (fractional anisotropy and apparent diffusion coefficient) and structural features as input to JOSA (which we call “JOSAConn”). Evaluated on HCP-YA subjects across 15 task contrasts, our method significantly outperforms FreeSurfer in functional alignment (Bonferroni-corrected p < 0.05 for 12 of 15 contrasts). This multimodal approach demonstrates that structural connectivity effectively bridges the gap between cortical geometry and functional organization while maintaining clinical applicability.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: External Spatial Adapter Tuning: Memory-Efficient Adaptation of Foundation Model for Sddh Diagnosis with Ultrasound Images.
abstract: Ultrasound-based computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) has indicated effectiveness for developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH). Recently, foundation models have shown promising potential to further improve the performance of a CAD model. However, their deployment in clinical applications remains challenging due to the high computational cost and overfitting risk of full fine-tuning. To address this issue, a new memory-efficient adaptation framework, named External Spatial Adapter Tuning (ESAT), is proposed for the CAD of DDH. The ESAT develops spatial adapters based on lowrank depthwise separable convolution at each layer of foundation model, so as to extract and refine hierarchical spatial features. These adapter outputs are further fused externally for the classification task, so that the gradient flow is fully decoupled from the foundation model. In real-world DDH diagnosis experiments, the ESAT requires only 30.16 % and 0.304 % of the memory and parameter usage on ViT-Base (as foundation model) compared with the full fine-tuning, yet achieves higher diagnostic accuracy than the full fine-tuning and other parameter-efficient tuning methods.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: DINOV3-Guided Cross Fusion Framework for Semantic-Aware CT Generation From MRI and CBCT.
abstract: Generating synthetic CT images from CBCT or MRI has a potential for efficient radiation dose planning and adaptive radiotherapy. However, existing CNN-based models lack global semantic understanding, while Transformers often overfit small medical datasets due to high model capacity and weak inductive bias. To address these limitations, we propose a DINOv3-Guided Cross Fusion (DGCF) framework that integrates a frozen self-supervised DINOv3 Transformer with a trainable CNN encoder-decoder. It hierarchically fuses global representation of Transformer and local features of CNN via a learnable cross fusion module, achieving balanced local appearance and contextual representation. Furthermore, we introduce a Multi-Level DINOv3 Perceptual (MLDP) loss that encourages semantic similarity between synthetic CT and the ground truth in DINOv3's feature space. Experiments on the SynthRAD2023 pelvic dataset demonstrate that DGCF achieved state-of-the-art performance in terms of MS-SSIM, PSNR and segmentation-based metrics on both MRI → CT and CBCT → CT translation tasks. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to employ DINOv3 representations for medical image translation, highlighting the potential of self-supervised Transformer guidance for semantic-aware CT synthesis. The code is available at https://github.com/HiLabgit/DGCF.git.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Adaptive Clinical-Aware Latent Diffusion for Multimodal Brain Image Generation and Missing Modality Imputation.
abstract: Multimodal neuroimaging provides complementary insights for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis, yet clinical datasets frequently suffer from missing modalities. We propose ACADiff, a framework that synthesizes missing brain imaging modalities through adaptive clinical-aware diffusion. ACADiff learns mappings between incomplete multimodal observations and target modalities by progressively denoising latent representations while attending to available imaging data and clinical metadata. The framework employs adaptive fusion that dynamically reconfigures based on input availability, coupled with semantic clinical guidance via GPT-4o-encoded prompts. Three specialized generators enable bidirectional synthesis among sMRI, FDG-PET, and AV45-PET. Evaluated on ADNI subjects, ACADiff achieves superior generation quality and maintains robust diagnostic performance even under extreme 80% missing scenarios, outperforming all existing baselines. To promote reproducibility, code is available at https://github.com/rongzhou7/ACADiff.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Joint Multiscale Image Learning for Segmentation in Macroscopic and Microscopic Pathology Images.
abstract: Image segmentation at both macroscopic and microscopic level is important in digital pathology. In these images, visually similar regions within the same image often share semantic characteristics, offering an opportunity for intra-image reference learning. We propose a novel binary segmentation framework using a joint multiscale image learning strategy. Our approach builds upon a whole image segmentation model and introduces a complementary part level module that enables mutual referencing among image regions. By computing the feature similarity, each target part image identifies its corresponding reference part images. Cross-attention is then applied between the target and reference part images to exchange information. This strategy not only enhances segmentation consistency but also increases the effective training sample size, improving generalization in small datasets. The proposed model significantly outperforms competitive methods in both macroscopic and microscopic datasets.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Personalized Federated Learning with Residual Fisher Information for Medical Image Segmentation.
abstract: Federated learning enables multiple clients (institutions) to collaboratively train machine learning models without sharing their private data. To address the challenge of data heterogeneity across clients, personalized federated learning (pFL) aims to learn customized models for each client. In this work, we propose pFL-ResFIM, a novel pFL framework that achieves client-adaptive personalization at the parameter level. Specifically, we introduce a new metric, Residual Fisher Information Matrix (ResFIM), to quantify the sensitivity of model parameters to domain discrepancies. To estimate ResFIM for each client model under privacy constraints, we employ a spectral transfer strategy that generates simulated data reflecting the domain styles of different clients. Based on the estimated ResFIM, we partition model parameters into domain-sensitive and domain-invariant components. A personalized model for each client is then constructed by aggregating only the domain-invariant parameters on the server. Extensive experiments on public datasets demonstrate that pFL-ResFIM consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, validating its effectiveness.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging

title: Mssanet: Multi-Scale Self-Attention Mechanism Network for Polyp Segmentation.
abstract: Accurate medical image segmentation is the foundation of effective diagnosis and treatment, and efficient polyp segmentation is particularly crucial in the early diagnosis of colorectal cancer. At present, many segmentation algorithms are based on deep learning. However, although convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are highly efficient, their ability to model long-distance dependencies is limited. Although the Transformer has powerful performance, its computational cost and the number of parameters is large. To alleviate these challenges, we have proposed an efficient multi-scale segmentation model (MSSANet) specifically tailored for polyp segmentation in colonoscopy images. Firstly, MSSF Module uses the attention mechanism to enhance spatial and positional information and integrate multi-scale information to emphasize pixel-level features, thereby improving spatial positional interaction. Secondly, a PSAK Module employ the partial attention mechanism and replace the traditional MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron) with KAN (Kolmogorov-Arnold Network) to reduce redundant parameters. The experimental results show that the MSSANet model exhibits good performance on datasets including CVC-300, CVC-ColonDB and ETIS.
conference_title: IEEE International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging
